battle.name: 第二次神聖戰爭
battle.brief: 公元前449至448年，雅典與斯巴達在阿提卡再起兵端：攝政王保薩尼阿斯率聯盟軍直抵厄琉西斯，雅典則以三百艘戰船掃掠伯羅奔尼撒海岸反擊，並圍困梅加拉。卡面的埃及月牙劍早已在愛琴海化為曲刃短刀，掛在重裝步兵與輕裝射手腰間。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 公元前449至448年的第二次神聖戰爭，交戰主體是雅典城邦與斯巴達城邦，但兩邊都不是國家，而是聯盟。雅典這一邊是提洛同盟：盟邦的分擔金與船隻攢在德里洛斯，公元前449年提洛同盟的金庫移往雅典，第一年的同盟貢金被留作軍費，戰時編制是十名輪流執行的將軍率領的重裝步兵方陣與三列槳戰船隊；雅典城本身人口數萬、外邦人居多，兵役按財產階層分級，超產者服役，無產者擔任划手與隨軍工匠。斯巴達這一邊是伯羅奔尼撒同盟：各邦按傳統出一份兵與一份錢，騎兵由三分之一的城邦湊出，指揮權握在兩位王與一批長老院成員以及五名監察官手中，攝政王保薩尼阿斯這次能單獨領兵進攻阿提卡，也沒有先取得斯巴達城邦的正式決議。站在雅典一邊的有伯羅奔尼撒南端的阿爾戈斯，中部傾向雅典的底比斯，以及在戰爭中與雅典結盟的塞薩利；站在斯巴達一邊的是科林斯，它以梅加拉受欺為由推動出兵；梅加拉本身是最直接的受害方，它的耕地被雅典反覆掠奪。戰區也牽涉到愛奧尼亞與西西里：雅典在戰前與西西里的隆提尼、塞革斯塔以及優卑亞的加爾基西亞簽約，薩摩斯起義幾乎與這場戰爭同時發生。最後要說明「神聖」這名號的由來：這不是宗教起義，古代文獻並未用「神聖戰爭」稱呼它，現代史家借第一次神聖戰爭（德爾斐聯盟對基拉）之名目借題，近代史上也曾以「基蒙的戰爭」稱之。
countriesEn: The Second Sacred War of 449–448 BC was fought between Athens and Sparta, though neither side was a state in the modern sense: each was an alliance. On the Athenian side stood the Delian League, whose tribute and ships were pooled at Delos; in 449 BC the league's treasury was moved to Athens and the first year's tribute was set aside for the war, and the command structure on campaign was a board of ten strategoi, elected by lot and rotated in command, directing a hoplite phalanx and a fleet of triremes. Athens itself was a city of tens of thousands of inhabitants with a large metic population; military service was graded by the property classes, the rich serving as hoplites, the poorer manning the oars and the baggage train. On the Spartan side stood the Peloponnesian League, whose members each contributed men and money in the traditional share, with cavalry furnished by one third of the member states; authority rested with the two kings, the gerousia and the five ephors, and the regent Pausanias was able to bring an army into Attica on his own initiative, without a formal decree of the Spartan state. On the Athenian side also stood Argos in the southern Peloponnese, Thebes in central Greece, which leaned toward Athens, and Thessaly, which allied with Athens during the war. On the Spartan side was Corinth, which pressed for an expedition on the strength of Megara's complaint; Megara itself was the most directly injured party, its farmland repeatedly ravaged by the Athenians. The war reached across the Aegean as well: Athens had concluded alliances with Leontini and Segesta in Sicily and with the Chalcidians in Euboea, and the revolt of Samos ran almost in parallel with it. Finally, the epithet: this was not a religious rising, and no ancient source calls it a Sacred War; the modern label borrows the name of the first Sacred War, the Amphictyonic conflict between Delphi and Cirrha, and older scholarship also called it the war of Cimon.
people: 留下姓名的關鍵人物不多，但每一位都把局面推向了下一個階段。雅典方面首推伯里克利：他以將軍身份統率主力，又在議事院與陪審法庭上主導政策。斯巴達使節到雅典要求解釋時，雅典人選了伯里克利與阿里斯提德（阿里斯提德之子）出來答話，兩人演說未完，斯巴達人便起身離去，隨即轉入攻勢。公元前448年，他以一百艘戰船與一萬五千名重裝步兵出海，在普拉提亞對全軍講話，再打到西基昂登陸，擊敗西基昂及其聯軍於野戰，最後直指科林斯地峽逼退斯巴達聯軍。斯巴達再入阿提卡時，他不與對方會戰，只把鄉民與牲畜撤入城牆、用艦隊在沿岸游弋騷擾，最後迫得對方退兵。他是這場戰爭中唯一沒有敗績的統帥，也是三十年和平最大的受益者。戲劇家索福克勒斯同樣掛著將軍的頭銜，他與伯里克利、拉克斯同率四十艘戰船赴薩摩斯平叛；拉克斯後來接手亞海防務，與薩摩斯的交涉也是他收尾。斯巴達方面，攝政王保薩尼阿斯之父普利斯托拿克斯正是普拉提亞之役的統帥；保薩尼阿斯因不滿伯里克利獨攬大權而樂見斯巴達出兵，逼迫不成便退回，後來遭斯巴達內部追究，逃亡到泰加，據說其後流亡底比斯而死於異鄉。他與斯巴達王普利斯托拿克斯一前一後都捲入受賄指控，攝政王被控受波斯賄賂而主張退兵，最終無罪獲釋，成為監察官制度上著名的醜聞。基蒙的名字也在其中：遠征西亞失利、同盟款項被指挪用，他據說在基提翁之圍中陣亡；政爭以伯里克利提出公訴、陪審團以五十票之差判基蒙無罪收場。
peopleEn: Few names survive from this war, but each of the men who left a mark pushed the situation into its next stage. First among the Athenians is Pericles: as a strategos he led the main body, and in the council and the law courts he set the policy. When the Spartan envoys came to demand an explanation, the Athenians chose Pericles and Aristides son of Lysimachus to answer them; the Spartans rose and left before the speeches were finished, and the Athenians immediately went on the offensive. In 448 BC Pericles took out a hundred ships and fifteen thousand hoplites, addressed the whole army at Plataea, landed and beat the Sicyonian and allied levy in a field battle, and then drove at the Isthmus of Corinth until the Spartan allies withdrew. When the Spartans entered Attica again, he declined to risk a pitched battle: he moved the rural population and the flocks behind the walls, used the fleet to harry the coast, and waited for the enemy to withdraw. He was the only commander of the war with an unbroken record, and the chief beneficiary of the Thirty Years' Peace. The tragedian Sophocles also held a general's commission; he sailed with Pericles and Laches in a fleet of forty ships to Samos, and Laches later took over the Aegean command and closed the arrangements with the island. On the Spartan side, the regent Pausanias was the son of Pleistoanax, the commander who had won Plataea against the Persians. Resentful of Pericles' growing predominance, Pausanias was glad to see the Spartans march into Attica to force an accommodation; when none came he withdrew, was later called to account at home, and fled to Tegea, and by later accounts ended his days in exile at Thebes. He and the Spartan king Pleistoanax were both drawn into a charge of bribery: the regent was accused of taking Persian money to persuade the Spartans to retire and was acquitted, an episode that became a standing scandal for the ephors. Cimon belongs to the cast as well: disgraced by the failure of the expedition to Syria and by the accusation of touching the allies' money, he is said to have died in the siege of Citium; the political struggle ended when Pericles prosecuted him and the jury acquitted him by only fifty votes.
kits: 卡面這件埃及月牙劍本身並沒有出現在公元前449年的戰場上，這點必須先講清楚。月牙劍是埃及自古王朝起就在使用的近身兵器，青銅質、單刃、刃口開在凸面，彎如新月，砍入甲冪或人身之後不必往回拔。到了第十八至第二王朝，它在埃及步兵手中已讓位給形制更省力的曲刃短刀。曲線並沒有停在埃及：同一條思路跨過地中海東岸進入愛琴海，就成了希臘重裝步兵與輕裝射手腰間那把彎刃單刀。也就是說，卡面這件月牙劍在這場戰爭裡的位置，是一把已經退役、但曲刃概念仍在役的祖型兵器：真正在希臘方陣裡砍殺的是它的下游產品，短柄、弧形、砍擊不需回抽。月牙的曲線在希臘還有另一個更直接的後代，就是輕裝兵手裡的月牙形小盾。於是這場戰爭的裝備骨架是這樣的：重裝步兵持圓盾、約兩米七的長槍、青銅頭盔、脛甲與胸甲，配一把曲刃短刀；輕裝兵與標槍手用月牙小盾與標槍；水師是三列槳戰船與登陸用划艇；攻城方面沒有攻城塔，也沒有拋石器，雅典對梅加拉用的是圍困加掠奪；海上有三百艘戰船的掃掠，陸上沒有大型工程器械，只有城牆本身的施工。還有一層值得寫：埃及在這場戰爭裡的位置。它當時是波斯的一個行省，卻是雅典糧食的重要來源之一，卡面這件兵器的故土，正以穀物而不是士兵的方式供應著這場戰爭。
kitsEn: The Egyptian khopesh on the card was not present on any battlefield in 449 BC, and that has to be said first. The khopesh was an Egyptian close-combat weapon in use from the Old Kingdom onwards: a bronze blade with a single edge on the convex side, curved like a new moon, which could be driven into a shield or a body and did not have to be pulled back out. By the Eighteenth and Twentieth Dynasties it had been displaced in Egyptian hands by a less effortful curved sword. The curve did not stop at Egypt: the same line of thinking, carried across the eastern Mediterranean into the Aegean, became the curved single-edged sword worn at the hip by the Greek hoplite and peltast. In other words, the position of the khopesh in this war is that of a retired ancestor whose curved concept was still in service: what actually cut and slashed in the Greek phalanx was its downstream descendant, short-hafted, arc-shaped, hacked in rather than thrust. The crescent of the khopesh has a second, more immediate heir in Greece, the small crescent-shaped shield carried by the light infantry. The equipment frame of this war is therefore: hoplites with the round aspis, a spear of about 2.7 metres, a bronze helmet, greaves and a cuirass, and a curved sword at the belt; light troops and javelinmen with the pelta and throwing spears; at sea, triremes and the landing boats. As for siege: this war saw no towers and no stone-throwers. Athens used blockade and devastation against Megara rather than assault, and there were no large engines on the land side, only the construction of the walls themselves. One more layer is worth recording: Egypt's position in this war. It was then a Persian satrapy, yet one of the great sources of Athens' grain, so the homeland of the card's weapon was supplying this war with grain rather than with soldiers.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術骨架是不決戰，以消耗與工程換對方的耐性。第一段是外交破裂：斯巴達攝政王保薩尼阿斯帶聯盟軍進入阿提卡，推進到厄琉西斯就停下，雅典全城戒備；斯巴達使節進城要求說明，雅典人推伯里克利與阿里斯提德出來答話，斯巴達人拒絕聽取就走了，戰端由此打開。第二段是攻勢而不是防守：三百艘戰船掃掠伯羅奔尼撒海岸，伯里克利率二十艘戰船與一萬名重裝步兵圍困梅加拉，把梅加拉人的田地反覆犁平，切斷其農業收入；同一時期第三道城牆（法勒魯姆方向）與第二道長牆的工程全力推進，攻城器械沒有出動，圍困代替了強攻。第三段是外線出擊：伯里克利以一百艘戰船與一萬五千名重裝步兵先在普拉提亞集結講話，再赴西基昂登陸，把西基昂聯軍擊敗於野戰，之後主力直指科林斯地峽，逼得斯巴達聯軍放棄地峽的守備。第四段是斯巴達的反制：公元前448年斯巴達軍再入阿提卡，雅典的應對是全城疏散，把鄉間人口與牲畜撤進城牆，主力不出城野戰，只用艦隊在沿岸游弋騷擾，同時在城牆上列陣待敵；斯巴達找不到可攻的城市，也沒能突破長牆，最後撤退，撤退的具體理由在古代與近代來源裡說法不一。第五段是收尾：薩摩斯問題在冬春之際解決，公元前446或445年，雅典與斯巴達議定三十年和平。整體看，這是海權對陸權、城牆對方陣的第一個完整樣本。
tacticsEn: The tactical skeleton of this war is: no decisive battle, but the trading of engineering and supplies for the enemy's patience. The first stage is the diplomatic rupture. The Spartan regent Pausanias led the allied army into Attica and halted at Eleusis; the Athenians manned the walls, and the Spartan envoys came into the city demanding an explanation. The Athenians put up Pericles and Aristides to speak for them, and the Spartans refused to listen and walked out; from that moment hostilities were open. The second stage is an offensive rather than a defence: three hundred ships swept the Peloponnesian coast, and Pericles with twenty ships and ten thousand hoplites blockaded Megara, ploughing its fields again and again to break Megarian agriculture, while the works on the third wall towards Phalerum and on the second Long Wall were pushed ahead at full speed. No siege engine was deployed; blockade took the place of assault. The third stage is the expedition outside Attica: Pericles took out a hundred ships and fifteen thousand hoplites, addressed the army at Plataea, landed at Sicyon and beat the Sicyonian league in a field battle, then drove the main body straight at the Isthmus of Corinth until the Spartan allies gave up their positions there. The fourth stage is the Spartan counterstroke: in 448 BC the Spartans entered Attica again, and the Athenian answer was to evacuate the countryside, move the population and the flocks behind the walls, keep the army inside and give no battle in the open, cruise with the fleet along the coast, and draw the hoplites up on the ramparts. The Spartans found no city they could take and could not breach the Long Walls, and in the end withdrew; ancient and later sources differ on the immediate reason. The fifth stage is the closing of the account: the Samian affair was settled in the winter and spring, and in 446 or 445 BC Athens and Sparta agreed a peace for thirty years. Taken as a whole, this is the first complete model of sea power against land power, and of the wall against the phalanx.
data: 可以核對的數字集中在修昔底德《伯羅奔尼撒戰爭史》第一卷，逐項列出並標明出處。年份：戰爭起於公元前449年，決於公元前448年，和約訂於公元前446或445年，古代的分年方式差一年。雅典的三項大規模出動：其一，三百艘戰船掃掠伯羅奔尼撒海岸（1.48）；其二，伯里克利以二十艘戰船與一萬名重裝步兵圍困梅加拉（1.48）；其三，一百艘戰船與一千名重裝步兵赴地峽督看築牆，再以五十艘戰船與三千名重裝步兵打西基昂與阿卡爾尼亞（1.49、1.51），其間夜營遭阿卡爾尼亞人襲擊，陣亡約三百人，連將軍在內（1.50）。最大的一次出動是公元前448年的一百艘戰船與一萬五千名重裝步兵（1.52）。薩摩斯平叛出動四十艘戰船（1.54）。長城工程：第一年一百艘船與一萬名重裝步兵，第二年起每年三千名重裝步兵與五十艘船（1.108）。阿提卡的守備總量可參亞里士多德《雅典政制》：重裝步兵約九千人，其中外邦人居四千人，騎兵一千六百人，三列槳戰船五百艘（23.1）。斯巴達方面，據狄奧多羅斯與亞里士多德所記，入侵兵力約三萬人，此為古代作者的概估，修昔底德本人未作詳載。地理尺度：雅典至厄琉西斯約十八公里，至梅加拉約四十公里，至科林斯地峽約六十五公里，阿提卡南北長約六十公里，長牆連同法勒魯姆方向一段合計約十公里；步兵每份口糧按五日份計算，行軍沿用五日份的標準。糧食方面，雅典的口糧多來自黑海與埃及方向，經塞浦路斯轉運入比雷埃夫斯。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are concentrated in the first book of Thucydides' History of the Peloponnesian War, and are set out here with their sources. Dates: the war began in 449 BC and was decided in 448 BC; the peace was concluded in 446 or 445 BC, ancient year-counting differing by one. Three large Athenian movements are recorded: three hundred ships sweeping the Peloponnesian coast (1.48); Pericles blockading Megara with twenty ships and ten thousand hoplites (1.48); and a hundred ships with a thousand hoplites sent to the Isthmus to supervise the wall, followed by fifty ships and three thousand hoplites against Sicyon and Acarnania (1.49 and 1.51), during which the night camp was surprised by the Acarnanians and about three hundred men were lost, the general among them (1.50). The largest movement was the hundred ships and fifteen thousand hoplites of 448 BC (1.52). The expedition to Samos used forty ships (1.54). For the Long Walls: in the first year a hundred ships and ten thousand hoplites, and from the second year each year three thousand hoplites and fifty ships (1.108). The overall strength of Athens may be taken from Aristotle's Constitution of the Athenians: roughly nine thousand hoplites, of whom four thousand were metics, sixteen hundred horsemen, and five hundred triremes (23.1). On the Spartan side, the invading force is given as about thirty thousand men by Diodorus and Aristotle; this is an ancient estimate, and Thucydides himself says no more. Distances: from Athens to Eleusis about eighteen kilometres, to Megara about forty, to the Isthmus about sixty-five; Attica is some sixty kilometres north to south; the Long Walls together with the Phalerum section amount to roughly ten kilometres of wall. A hoplite's ration was reckoned in days of provisions, five days being the usual standard for a marching army. On supplies, Athens drew much of its grain from the Black Sea and from Egypt, transhipped through Cyprus and brought into Piraeus.
cause: 打起來的直接原因有兩條，一條是阿提卡的牆，一條是梅加拉的田。梅加拉夾在雅典與科林斯之間，土地被兩面擠壓；雅典在提洛同盟的稅收安排落定之後，藉口自衛需要把梅加拉人的部分領土收走，逼迫梅加拉人遷往雅典。梅加拉人跑到科林斯哭訴，科林斯人以此為由鼓動斯巴達出兵。另一條原因是長牆：斯巴達人眼看雅典人正用石頭把城與海連起來，等於把比雷埃夫斯變成城牆之內的港口，這在伯羅奔尼撒同盟看來是把整個希臘的入口握在一人之手，於是保衛希臘人自由成了出兵的說法，公元前446年的和約文本正是用這句話收尾。但古史家又補了一筆：這次入侵很可能有雅典人自己的推手，修昔底德明確記載，斯巴達軍之所以前進，據說是雅典人希望斯巴達去對付波斯人對赫勒斯滂的威脅；動機如何姑且不論，結果一樣，兩邊的舊帳一起被翻了出來。深層原因是帝國與霸權的對撞：雅典靠提洛同盟的貢金養著帝國，斯巴達靠同盟的份額維持城邦體系，兩套帳目在同一片愛琴海上互相看不順眼，第一次波斯戰爭的戰時同盟本來就靠共同的敵人維持，敵人一旦退場，盟約就失去了存在的理由。
causeEn: There are two immediate causes of the fighting, one a wall and one a field. Megara lay between Athens and Corinth with its land squeezed from both sides; once the tribute arrangements of the Delian League were settled, Athens took a strip of Megarian territory under the pretext of self-defence and pushed the Megarians to emigrate to Athens. The Megarians went to Corinth with their complaint, and the Corinthians used it to press the Spartans into sending out an army. The second cause is the Long Walls: seeing Athens join stone between the city and the sea, making the Piraeus a port inside a fortification, the Peloponnesian League came to think that one man was taking hold of the entrance to all Greece, and the freedom of the Hellenes became the stated reason for the expedition, the very phrase with which the peace of 446 BC closes. The historians add a qualification: the invasion may have been pushed by Athens itself, for Thucydides states plainly that the Spartans advanced, as it was said, at the wish of the Athenians, who wanted them to hold the Persians off the Hellespont. Whatever the motive, the result was the same, and old accounts were opened all at once. The deeper cause is the collision of empire with hegemony: Athens supported its empire with the tribute of the Delian League, Sparta supported its system with the contributions of its own league, the two sets of accounts had never met comfortably on the same Aegean, and the wartime alliance of the Persian Wars had only ever been held together by a common enemy. Once the enemy withdrew, the alliance had no reason to exist.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果，是雅典的海上帝國獲得了完整的陸地防衛。第一件事：長牆與第三道牆完工，雅典城從此是一座要塞式的城，牆內住著幾萬人，牆外有城邦的艦隊。亞里士多德後來批評這種形勢讓雅典人變得鬆散，把城中的女人、孩子與閒人算作全體民力的錯；這種鬆散是事後的譴責，倒說明當時的人為何肯忍。城牆一立，希臘世界此後的戰爭規則就變了：城邦的實力在海軍而不在陸軍，雅典的戰略從此是把敵人拖到海上、用錢而不是用血去贏。第二件事：斯巴達的聲望跌到谷底，攝政王未戰而退、國王被控受賄而無罪、兩度進攻阿提卡都沒有打下雅典城，這些都被喜劇作家在《利西斯特拉特》裡拿來取笑，數十年後伯里克利在演說中仍用來提醒雅典人不要怕斯巴達。第三件事：基蒙的政治生命就此結束，遠征西亞的敗績、同盟款項的指責、與伯里克利的黨爭，讓這位歐律墨冬的英雄退場，雅典的政策從此由伯里克利一人的路線定調，帝國的形態、海軍的規模、城牆的樣式都按這條路線定型。第四件事：薩摩斯問題以可控方式收束，雅典在島上推行移民屯田，島嶼被納入帝國的行政與海軍編制，成為後來雅典對付愛琴海諸島的樣板。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the war was that the Athenian maritime empire acquired a complete landward defence. First: with the Long Walls and the third wall finished, Athens became a city that was a fortress, tens of thousands of people living inside the circuit and the fleet of a polis outside it. Aristotle later blamed this arrangement for the softness of the Athenians, counting the women, the children and the idle among the total strength of the city; that the complaint was made only afterwards shows how much the citizens were willing to endure at the time. Once the walls stood, the rules of war in the Greek world changed: a city's strength lay in its fleet rather than its army, and the Athenian strategy became that of dragging the enemy out to sea and winning with money rather than with blood. Second: the standing of Sparta fell to its lowest point. A regent who withdrew without a battle, a king acquitted on a charge of taking bribes, two invasions of Attica that did not take Athens: Aristophanes used all of it for comedy in the Lysistrata, and Pericles could still refer to it decades later to tell the Athenians not to fear the Spartans. Third: Cimon's public life ended here. The failed expedition to Syria, the accusation of touching the allies' money, and the factional struggle with Pericles removed the hero of the Eurymedon from the stage; from then on Athenian policy was set by Pericles' line alone, and the shape of the empire, the scale of the fleet and the form of the walls were all fixed to that line. Fourth: the Samian affair was closed in a manageable way, with a cleruchy settled on the island, bringing Samos into the administrative and naval order of the empire and serving as a model for Athens' handling of the Aegean islands thereafter.
result: 公元前448年夏，斯巴達聯軍第二次撤出阿提卡，戰爭以沒有會戰的方式收場。雅典沒有攻入伯羅奔尼撒，沒有奪取科林斯的港口，沒有擊毀斯巴達的方陣；斯巴達也沒有攻破雅典的城牆，沒有奪得一寸牆外的土地，連一座像樣的遠征營帳都沒能留到季末。結果是一份維持現狀的和平：公元前446或445年，兩方同意各自放棄戰時所得，斯巴達承認其他希臘人的獨立，雅典保留提洛同盟的貢金、艦隊與長牆，第三方城市如梅加拉取回被奪走的耕地，但要在牆上留出雅典指定的缺口供人出入。這份和約有效期三十年，是伯羅奔尼撒戰爭之前希臘世界最長的一段穩定期，也把雅典的帝國與斯巴達的霸權同時固定下來。對雙方而言，這是一場各自都沒有輸的戰爭：斯巴達保住了表面上的均勢，雅典保住了實質上的城牆與海。真正輸掉的是第三種可能，即兩家在沒有外敵的年代裡學會共處。公元前431年，長期摩擦的計時重新啟動，這段三十年的空白，最後只是一個被拉長了的間隙。
resultEn: In the summer of 448 BC the Spartan allies withdrew from Attica for the second time, and the war ended without a battle. Athens did not invade the Peloponnese, did not take a Corinthian port, and did not break a Spartan phalanx; the Spartans did not breach the Athenian walls, did not win an inch of land beyond them, and did not keep a campaigning camp alive to the end of the season. The result was a peace that froze the situation: in 446 or 445 BC the two sides agreed each to give up what had been won in the war, Sparta recognised the independence of the other Hellenes, and Athens kept the tribute, the fleet and the Long Walls of the Delian League; third parties such as Megara recovered the land they had lost, but had to leave gaps in their walls at points the Athenians specified. The treaty was to run for thirty years, and it was the longest stretch of stability in the Greek world before the Peloponnesian War, fixing the Athenian empire and the Spartan hegemony at the same time. For both sides it was a war in which neither had lost: Sparta kept the appearance of a balance, Athens kept the substance of walls and sea. What was lost was a third possibility, that the two city-states would learn to live with each other in the years when they had no common enemy. In 431 BC the long counting of mutual friction started again, and this thirty-year interval proved to be no more than an extended pause.
